html:
Zeno of Citium was a philosopher, born around 334 BCE in Kition on Cyprus, who founded the Stoic school in Athens around 300 BCE.

A merchant's son, he is said to have come to Athens after a shipwreck and to have studied with the Cynic Crates. He taught in the Stoa Poikile, the painted porch on the Agora, which gave Stoicism its name. He taught that virtue is the only good, that people should live in agreement with nature and reason, and that all humans are citizens of one world. Stoicism shaped the Roman elite, from Seneca to Marcus Aurelius, and early Christian thought. Athens honoured Zeno with a public tomb. His books are lost, known only through later writers.
sum: Zeno of Citium was a philosopher, born around 334 BCE in Kition on Cyprus, who founded the Stoic school in Athens around 300 BCE.
